title: decision.json v1 records (6/23–8/09) carried no decision-time state on commits and dropped the skip's second candidate
tier_reason: research-data provenance gap: the records written 6/23–8/09 cannot say which streak/saver state fed each commit (recoverable only by ledger as-of joins) and skip→double intents cannot be verified; no delivery, entry, grading or alerting effect — the scoreable gate and skip-policy shadow use only fields v1 kept

contract.text: Every final decision record persists the state that fed the decision (streak, saver_available, state_source, state_status, allow_double, contest_source_date) and, on skips, the executable second candidate.
contract.source: 5216ea1 (bts_daily_decision_v2); docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-09-boundary-shadow-measurement.md 'Follow-up (separate, production): bts_daily_decision_v2' — note: this contract dates from 8/09; the v1 contract (docs/audit/2026-06-20-skip-policy-shadow.md) required streak/saver and the single executable candidate on MDP skips only

mechanism.text: the v1 writer persisted streak/saver only on MDP skip records and recorded no state source/status or allow_double anywhere, so commit records carried no decision-time state (the census counted 31 of 44 records state-null)

code.symbol: run_and_pick (DecisionStreakState not threaded to the record)

mechanism.text: SelectionResult carried the executable second candidate, but both skip-capture sites dropped it when writing the skip record, so a skip whose declined intent was a double cannot be verified from the record

residual.text: The fix is prospective: v1 records for 6/23–8/09 stay state-null on commits and lack skip second candidates; analyses must recover state from ledger/saver as-of joins or exclude the rows (state_source = unknown).
residual.source: 5216ea1 body ('from the first deploy onward'); boundary-shadow spec §Census (state_source recorded / ledger_asof / unknown)

watchdog.trigger: a finalized decision.json (commit or skip) that lacks any v2 provenance field, or a skip record whose declined intent is a double without its second candidate, written after the v2 deploy
watchdog.recovery_assertion: every final record for the date validates against bts_daily_decision_v2's required fields and load_decision accepts it

evidence.what: v1 records were unusable as a state source (only MDP skips persisted streak/saver), skip records lost the executable second candidate (carried by SelectionResult, dropped at capture), and nothing recorded which state stream fed the decision; v2 persists all of it prospectively
31/44 decision records are state-null; only the 13 MDP skips persist streak/saver (census count over box records, not re-read here)
skip→double intents are flagged non-executable-verifiable because v1 skip records carry no second candidate
the v1 design recorded, for genuine skips, the executable declined candidate plus streak/saver as context; commit-record state was not part of it
pre-deploy 64f0ffb -> deployed 0e4aaa8 at 2026-08-10T02:00:22Z, canary passed: first v2 writer install

notes: arguably a design limitation, not a defect: v1 met its documented contract; the gap was exposed by a new research use (the 8/09 boundary-shadow census). It does not matter to W4 watchdog or restore coverage — the lead may drop it or treat 5216ea1 as a feature; the one capture-omission element is link 2 (data held in SelectionResult but not written)

exposure: v1 records from the first decision.json (6/23) to the v2 install (8/10 02:00:22Z); defective ref cites the installed tree 64f0ffb (log 8/10 00:41Z → 02:00Z; only docs/spec commits before 5216ea1^ = 6db921c)
watchdog boundary 'preservation' is a forced fit (decision records as the preserved audit trail); no operational boundary applies
the census's action-diff counts and dates are research results; not restated
